newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: China premier Li Peng to visit Malaysia this year.
newsitem.headline: China premier Li Peng to visit Malaysia this year.

text.p: China's Prime Minister Li Peng has accepted an invitation to visit Malaysia this year to further enhance Sino-Malaysian relations, Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi said on Saturday.
Abdullah, who is in Beijing for a three-day official visit, was quoted by the national news agency Bernama as saying that the actual date of Li's trip was being worked out.

The premier's preliminary itinerary in Malaysia would include meeting represenatives of Malaysia's private sector, Abdullah told Bernama by telephone from Beijing. The Malaysian minister is leaving today for a six-day visit to North Korea.
During his meeting with Li, Abdullah said the Chinese premier expressed satisfaction that China and Malaysia enjoyed sound bilateral relations with the high-level exchange of visits.
On the disputed Spratly Islands, Li explained that China would resolve conflicting issues peacefully based on international law and the laws of the sea, Abdullah said.
He said China hoped the area would remain peaceful and stable for the good of the region's economic development.
The Spratlys, a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals in the South China Sea, are claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Brunei, the Philippines, Malaysia and Vietnam.

Abdullah earlier signed and exchanged documents with his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen on the Malaysian diplomatic mission in Hong Kong becoming a consulate from July 1, when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule.
